claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Vending-Bench is a simulated environment designed to test an LLM-based agent's ability to manage a long-running vending machine business.
claims.quote: In this paper, we present Vending-Bench, a simulated environment designed to specifically test an LLM-based agent's ability to manage a straightforward, long-running business scenario: operating a vending machine.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: In Vending-Bench, agents must balance inventories, place orders, set prices, and handle daily fees over long horizons exceeding 20M tokens per run.
claims.quote: Agents must balance inventories, place orders, set prices, and handle daily fees - tasks that are each simple but collectively, over long horizons (>20M tokens per run) stress an LLM's capacity for sustained, coherent decision-making.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Experiments show high variance: Claude 3.5 Sonnet and o3-mini manage the machine well in most runs and turn a profit, but all models have runs that derail through misinterpreting delivery schedules, forgetting orders, or meltdown loops.
claims.quote: Our experiments reveal high variance in performance across multiple LLMs: Claude 3.5 Sonnet and o3-mini manage the machine well in most runs and turn a profit, but all models have runs that derail, either through misinterpreting delivery schedules, forgetting orders, or descending into tangential "meltdown" loops from which they rarely recover.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: The source reports no clear correlation between failures and the point at which the model's context window becomes full, suggesting breakdowns do not stem from memory limits.
claims.quote: We find no clear correlation between failures and the point at which the model's context window becomes full, suggesting that these breakdowns do not stem from memory limits.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: LLMs can perform well on isolated short-term tasks but often fail to maintain coherent performance over longer time horizons.
claims.quote: While Large Language Models (LLMs) can exhibit impressive proficiency in isolated, short-term tasks, they often fail to maintain coherent performance over longer time horizons.

claims.question: q4
claims.claim: Vending-Bench also tests models' ability to acquire capital, framed as a necessity in many hypothetical dangerous AI scenarios.
claims.quote: Apart from highlighting the high variance in performance over long time horizons, Vending-Bench also tests models' ability to acquire capital, a necessity in many hypothetical dangerous AI scenarios.
